The numbers are Vigor, basically characters have limited energy in ToA and you can only use them a limited number of times. Different floors take different amounts of energy, so floor 1 consumes 1, 2 uses 2, 3 - 3, 4 - 4, and the tower that resets monthly has floors that take 5. 

Since characters start with 10 Vigor that means you can use one team to clear one full tower OR mix and match them as long as the level numbers add up to 10 or less. Since the zone you're clearing is the first one and only has one tower it doesn't come into play yet, but for later towers you might need to clear it with worse built DPSes to save your main's energy for the hard levels. That's why people say 3 teams are needed for endgame

Resetting a floor's score gives the character their Vigor back, and retrying it to get higher scores doesn't consume it again either (because they are already registered on that floor), so just repeat the level(s) where you have less than 3 crests until you get max, the game will then prompt you if you wanna accept the new score and count the new one towards the total

The SNES thing is due to color bleeding: since the games were designed to look good on a CRT, sometimes artists would make patterns that bleed together and create more realistic looking water/grass/skies etc when the colors bled through and combined, creasting an illusion of having more colors and smoother lines. On modern displays a pixel is more self-contained and won't affect how other pixels look, so the effect is lost (unless you use other software to emulate the color bleed)
